summary: Register lists a Houston County Nogalus tower as gone; a lookout directory files it under Trinity County. No source found describes the site.

facts.status_note: Register lists the tower as gone. No source found describes what remains at the site.

events.note: Register lists the tower as gone. It gives no build date, removal date or cause.

evidence.supports: Register row for the Nogalus tower: Houston County, coordinates, marked Tower Gone
Map listing carries the name Nogalus Lookout Tower for a tower in Houston County
Topozone page is the list of towers in Houston County, where the Nogalus entry appears
Lookout directory files Nogalus under Trinity County
Book describes the location and design of Texas lookout towers
evidence.quote: it describes the location and design of the lookout towers and associated structures in Texas

evidence.supports: Book published by Texas A&M University Press in May 2025

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and the Topozone map listing place Nogalus in Houston County. Central US Lookouts files it under Trinity County. The story follows the register and says the sources do not settle the county.

sources.title: Fire in the Piney Woods: Texas Lookout Towers, the Forest Service, and the Civilian Conservation Corps

notes_for_editor: Thinnest of the three. The only Nogalus-specific facts are the register row, a map-database name and a county label on a page that gives only the name and county. The body is about 127 words, just over the 120-word floor. The Trinity/Houston county conflict is unresolved; the story keeps Houston. Map-database entries show a name, not a structure, so the 'today' paragraph says nothing is known about the site. Verify county against Texas land or county records before publishing. Searches found no Nogalus history.
